Re: 
Transmission Owner Tariff Revisions of San Diego Gas & Electric Company  
Docket No.  ER27-___-000 
 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
 
Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C.  § 824d, and Part 35 
of the Regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”), 
San Diego Gas & Electric Company (“SDG&E”) hereby submits proposed revisions to its 
Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”) to address concerns raised in the Order to Show Cause 
issued in Docket No.  EL26-71-000 on June 18, 2026.1  The proposed revisions expand upon 
existing procedures in SDG&E’s TO Tariff to establish the terms and conditions applicable to 
requests for transmission-level interconnection and transmission service by Eligible Customers on 
behalf of Large Loads (“ECLL”)2 utilizing SDG&E-owned transmission facilities under the 
operational control of the California Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”).  The 
revisions amend Sections 3 (Definitions), 5 (Access Charges and Transmission Rates), 8 
(Obligation to Interconnect), 9 (Expansion Process), and 10 (Interconnection Process) of the TO 
Tariff, and add a pro forma Study Agreement (Appendix XIII) and a pro forma Interconnection 
Agreement (“IA”) (Appendix XIV). 
 
The tariff revisions proposed in this filing respond to the concerns expressed in the Show 
Cause Order regarding the interconnection of, and provision of service to, an ECLL.  These

concerns include the need for transparent and workable application and study procedures, 
appropriate operational requirements, a mechanism that allows for partial energization of Large 
Loads pending completion of network upgrades, and measures designed to ensure that costs 
associated with interconnections do not create the possibility of unwarranted cost shifting to other 
transmission customers.  The tariff revisions proposed in this Section 205 filing establish a defined 
framework under which SDG&E will receive and process requests for service from ECLLs.  Under 
this framework, SDG&E will perform the studies necessary to identify facilities required to 
accommodate those requests, apply security provisions that protect other transmission ratepayers 
from the possibility of undue cost shifts, and establish other requirements associated with 
interconnection to SDG&E-owned transmission facilities. 
 
With respect to cost shift protection specifically, based on ongoing discussions among 
other CAISO Participating Transmission Owners (“PTOs”) and SDG&E’s understanding of other 
PTOs’ approaches for mitigating cost shifting risks, SDG&E believes its approach is substantively 
aligned with that of Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) and DesertLink, LLC (“LS 
Power”).  The SDG&E, SCE, and LS Power frameworks all require initial security tied to the cost 
of the network upgrades that the PTO determines are necessary to interconnect Eligible Customers 
requesting interconnection service on behalf of Large Loads.  Each also provides that the PTO will 
draw on the security in the event the Large Load ceases operation or provides an amount of 
transmission revenues that is less than what is necessary to offset the cost of the network upgrades, 
considering the long-term benefits such upgrades provide to all transmission ratepayers.   
 
Indeed, discussions between SDG&E and others in California in the months since the 
issuance of the Show Cause Order addressed a far broader range of topics than the important 
questions concerning cost shift mitigation.  SDG&E developed its proposed tariff revisions after 
consultation with the CAISO and the other PTOs, and in recognition of the respective and 
complementary responsibilities of CAISO and the PTOs for transmission service and 
interconnections to the CAISO Controlled Grid.  Under the proposed framework, SDG&E, as the 
Transmission Owner (“TO”) under its TO Tariff, will administer the application and study process 
for requests involving SDG&E-owned transmission facilities, while coordinating with CAISO 
with respect to matters affecting the reliability and operation of the CAISO Controlled Grid.  This 
coordination is necessary because ECLL interconnections may require modifications to 
transmission facilities under CAISO operational control where such modifications are identified 
by SDG&E outside of the CAISO’s annual Transmission Planning Process (“TPP”).  Such 
modifications also may affect the reliable operation of the broader CAISO Controlled Grid. 
 
The proposed revisions are just and reasonable because they establish a transparent, 
durable, and nondiscriminatory framework for processing transmission-level requests on behalf of 
new Large Loads while addressing the reliability and cost-shifting concerns identified by the 
Commission in the Show Cause Order.  The revisions provide consistency between SDG&E’s TO 
Tariff and the corresponding CAISO tariff framework while preserving the respective 
responsibilities of SDG&E as a PTO and the CAISO as operator of the Balancing Authority Area 
in which SDG&E’s transmission facilities are located.

Hon. Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
November 16, 2026 
Page 3 of 25 
 
SDG&E respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed tariff revisions as 
described herein, effective February 16, 2027, and terminate the show cause proceeding in Docket 
No.  EL26-71-000 as to SDG&E. 
 
I. 
BACKGROUND 
 
A.   
SDG&E and Its TO Tariff 
 
SDG&E is a California public utility corporation with its principal place of business at 
8330 Century Park Court, San Diego, California 92123.  SDG&E provides electric transmission, 
distribution, and other energy services in San Diego and Orange Counties, California, subject to 
the respective jurisdictions of this Commission and the California Public Utilities Commission 
(“CPUC”).  SDG&E, has transferred operational control of its transmission facilities to the CAISO 
and is an Original PTO in the CAISO.  SDG&E’s transmission facilities subject to CAISO’s 
Operational Control are part of the CAISO Controlled Grid.   
 
SDG&E’s TO Tariff sets forth SDG&E’s Transmission Revenue Requirement and the rates 
and charges for access to the CAISO Controlled Grid.  The TO Tariff also governs requests for 
physical interconnection to the SDG&E-owned components of the CAISO Controlled Grid by 
entities eligible to request interconnection consistent with FPA section 210(a).  Interconnection of 
wholesale generation is governed by the CAISO Tariff, and interconnections requested by entities 
not eligible under section 210(a) remain subject to the Local Regulatory Authority. 
 
B.   
The Show Cause Order 
 
The Show Cause Order recognized that, in CAISO, an Eligible Customer submits an 
interconnection application to the PTO, which performs the studies needed to interconnect new 
load, and the Eligible Customer then retains a Scheduling Coordinator to obtain transmission 
service from CAISO.3  The Commission there found that the TO Tariffs generally do not explain 
the details of the study processes or the technical and reliability considerations in the studies for 
requests by Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads.  Accordingly, it directed CAISO and the 
PTOs to explain whether their tariffs remain just and reasonable without, among other things: 
 
• 
a definition of large load; 
• 
an application process that accepts applications on a rolling basis, with a non-
refundable application fee and readiness requirements that escalate at distinct 
phases of the study process; 
• 
information and data requirements regarding the characteristics of the large load, 
including disclosure of substantially similar pending requests on behalf of the same 
large load; 
• 
study procedures that evaluate the risks presented by large load behavior, including 
supplemental studies, and that recognize loads willing and able to limit their 
withdrawals; 
 
3  
Show Cause Order at pp. 19-20.

Hon. Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
November 16, 2026 
Page 4 of 25 
 
• 
ongoing operational requirements, memorialized in pro forma agreements; and 
• 
a cost recovery agreement requiring a minimum contribution toward the 
transmission owner’s transmission revenue requirement, backed by credit support, 
with payments and security draws credited to the transmission revenue 
requirement. 
 
The Commission invited CAISO and the PTOs to submit proposals in response to the Order or in 
an FPA Section 205 filing designed to address the concerns expressed in the Show Cause Order, 
tailored to their unique circumstances.  This filing is SDG&E’s proposal. 
 
II. 
PROPOSED INTERCONNECTION PROCESS REFORMS 
 
The Show Cause Order identifies concern with the lack of “clear and consistent” tariff 
provisions governing requests for service by Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads.  SDG&E 
addresses this concern directly through the development of new and enhanced procedures 
governing service requests by Eligible Customers under the TO Tariff.  SDG&E’s proposed tariff 
revisions do not ask the Commission or stakeholders to learn entirely new vocabulary.  Instead, 
SDG&E’s framework borrows the familiar architecture of generator interconnection, which the 
Commission and market participants already understand well and that has been found to be just 
and reasonable, and applies it to Eligible Customers requesting service on behalf of large loads.  
Elements of SDG&E’s proposed framework include: (1) an application process featuring a time-
stamped queue, a scoping meeting, and a Site Control requirement including allowance for 
deposits in lieu of Site Control; (2) sequential study phases with defined timelines and deposits, 
and a single amendment right; and, (3) pro forma interconnection agreement with milestones, 
options for limited operation pending completion of upgrades, financial security and possible 
withdrawals, and queue forfeiture upon default. 
 
The proposed framework also reflects the complementary roles of SDG&E as a PTO and 
the CAISO.  SDG&E owns the relevant transmission facilities and will administer the 
interconnection process established under its TO Tariff.  The CAISO operates the CAISO 
Controlled Grid and is vested with responsibility for matters assigned to it under the Transmission 
Control Agreement and the CAISO Tariff.  For instance, interconnection service under the TO 
Tariff is not the same thing as and does not supplant transmission service governed by CAISO’s 
tariff; rather, the interconnection customer requesting transmission service over the CAISO 
Controlled Grid must take such service from CAISO through a Scheduling Coordinator.  
SDG&E’s proposed pro forma Interconnection Agreement confirms this point (Article 4.3).  
Additionally, the proposed procedures provide for coordination between SDG&E and the CAISO 
where necessary to secure the CAISO’s concurrence that the transmission upgrades identified by 
SDG&E through its study process are not duplicative of transmission upgrades the CAISO has 
identified through its annual TPP, and that the upgrades and operational requirements identified 
by SDG&E through its study process are consistent with safe and reliable operation of the CAISO 
Controlled Grid (pro forma IA, Article 5.5.2). 
 
Importantly, the proposed revisions are limited to matters properly addressed through 
SDG&E’s Commission-jurisdictional TO Tariff.  They do not alter the respective federal and state

Hon. Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
November 16, 2026 
Page 5 of 25 
 
jurisdictional responsibilities applicable to retail electric service.  Nor do they change the class of 
customers eligible to receive Commission-jurisdictional transmission service under SDG&E’s TO 
Tariff.  Rather, the revisions establish the procedures and requirements applicable when an Eligible 
Customer seeks to interconnect its facilities with SDG&E-owned transmission from SDG&E as a 
TO in order for it – the Eligible Customer – to serve the Large Load directly.  Indeed, while the 
reforms proposed here are motivated by SDG&E’s desire to address points in the Show Cause 
Order regarding Eligible Customers requesting service on behalf of large loads, many of the 
reforms proposed herein will be broadly applicable to other categories of Eligible Customer service 
requests under SDG&E’s TO Tariff.   
 
A. 
Definition of Large Load 
 
The Show Cause Order at P 57 states that CAISO and PTO tariffs “lack a definition of 
large load, as a new category of load[,]” and suggests that “[a]n appropriate definition, including 
a load size and interconnection voltage threshold, should be based on the characteristics of 
CAISO’s transmission system.”  The Show Cause Order suggests that a reasonable definition 
would be “a new commercial or industrial customer, located at a single site behind one or more 
points of interconnection, and that has a peak load of 50 MW or greater, interconnects to the 
transmission system at a voltage level of greater than 69 kV, and is not part of a co-location 
arrangement.”  Rather than adopt the Show Cause Order’s definition, SDG&E proposes to include 
the following definition of “Large Load” in its TO Tariff: “a new customer, located at a single site 
behind one or more points of interconnection to the CAISO Controlled Grid, and that has a peak 
load of 50 MW or greater.”4   
 
SDG&E’s proposed definition differs from the definition in the Show Cause Order in three 
respects.  First, in SDG&E’s view, the Show Cause Order’s call out to “commercial and industrial 
customers” is not necessary because, as a practical matter, SDG&E expects that loads of 50 MW 
or greater will likely fall into these two general categories of customers.  Second, SDG&E believes 
that the express call-out to the CAISO Controlled Grid in its definition is preferable to the general 
reference to the “transmission system” in the Show Cause Order definition.  This call-out is 
necessary because some sub-transmission facilities within the CAISO Balancing Authority Area 
are operated at voltages greater than 69 kV but are not part of the CAISO Controlled Grid, while 
certain of SDG&E’s transmission facilities that are part of the CAISO Controlled Grid operate at 
69 kV.  Thus, the Show Cause Order definition is both over- and under-inclusive relative to 
SDG&E’s proposed definition.  Finally, SDG&E’s proposed definition does not exclude Large 
Loads that may be co-located with generation.  In SDG&E’s view, such an exclusion could limit 
the ratepayer protections that are a key feature of SDG&E’s proposed framework. 
 
B. 
Application Process 
 
The Show Cause Order at P 58 states that CAISO and PTO tariffs “lack sufficiently clear 
and consistent provisions establishing the application process and study procedures that will be 
used when CAISO and/or the Participating Transmission Owners evaluate the provision of

Hon. Debbie-Anne A. Reese

transmission service to Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads.”  The Show Cause Order 
identifies a rolling application process, non-refundable application fee and escalating readiness 
requirements, and requirements to provide to the PTO and/or CAISO regarding the large load as 
elements the Commission believes should be reflected in the CAISO and PTO tariffs. 
 
Discussed in the following subsections are SDG&E’s proposed tariff revisions to address 
these concerns. 
 
1. 
Intake and Initiating the Study Process 
 
Section 10 of SDG&E’s TO Tariff already includes an application process and study 
procedures for Eligible Customer service requests.  In this filing, SDG&E proposes substantial 
reforms to this existing framework, including through the following modifications: 
 
• 
Rolling applications.  The existing TO Tariff interconnection process is serial in nature 
and does not include any “windows” during which applications must be submitted.  
Accordingly, SDG&E already accepts applications at any time on a rolling basis.  To 
address the Commission’s suggestion regarding the need for an application process that 
accepts applications on a rolling basis, SDG&E proposes to maintain its current serial study 
process that accepts and studies each application at any time on a rolling basis, with priority 
based on the date SDG&E, as the PTO, receives the application.  SDG&E has modified 
Section 10.2 of the TO Tariff to state clearly that applications shall be accepted on a rolling 
basis.  As part of its framework to deter speculative or duplicative requests discussed in the 
Readiness Requirements section below, SDG&E proposes a $50,000 non-refundable 
application fee, also in Section 10.2. 
• 
Scoping Meeting.  SDG&E has added language to Section 10.3 of the TO Tariff 
establishing a Scoping Meeting that may occur following receipt of the application fee but 
before commencement of the System Impact Study.  The Scoping Meeting is proposed to 
occur at the request of either SDG&E or the Interconnection Customer for the purpose of 
discussing interconnection options and refining information and models. 
• 
Single pro forma Study Agreement.  SDG&E proposes a pro forma Study Agreement 
that is referenced in and attached to its TO Tariff (Appendix XIII).  The Study Agreement 
establishes the terms and conditions applicable to the System Impact Study and, as 
applicable, subsequent Facilities and Electromagnetic Transient (“EMT”) Studies.  In 
particular, the Study Agreement treats sixty (60) calendar days as the default good faith 
estimate for each of the System Impact and Facilities Studies.  Appendix XIII, Section 8.0. 
The use of a single pro forma Study Agreement streamlines the study process by 
eliminating the need to separately tender, negotiate, and execute a new agreement between 
study phases, thereby reducing administrative delays and facilitating more timely 
progression of the required studies.  In addition, assuming Commission acceptance of the 
pro forma Study Agreement, execution of conforming Study Agreements would not 
require individual filings with, and acceptance by, the Commission.  This will allow the 
applicable study to proceed without the need for specific Commission action, thereby 
reducing potential delays for customers.  After providing the required notice and study

deposit, an applicant may immediately proceed to the next applicable study phase under 
the existing Study Agreement. 
Additional details concerning the study process itself are set forth below.   
 
2. 
Readiness Requirements 
 
To deter speculative or duplicative requests and ensure that projects progressing through 
the study process continue to demonstrate readiness, SDG&E proposes a readiness framework that 
includes both upfront financial commitments and ongoing project-development milestones.  
Specifically, SDG&E proposes a $50,000 non-refundable application fee, an initial $100,000 
deposit for the System Impact Study, an additional $100,000 deposit if the applicant elects to 
proceed with a Facilities Study, and an additional $200,000 study deposit if SDG&E determines 
that an EMT Study is required.5  Each study deposit will be applied toward the actual cost of the 
applicable study and will be subject to reconciliation in accordance with the Study Agreement. 
 
SDG&E would also require an ECLL applicant to identify a definitive Point of 
Interconnection to the CAISO Controlled Grid.  In addition, the proposed TO Tariff revisions 
include provisions governing an applicant’s demonstration of Site Control, including a limited 
opportunity to provide documentation and a deposit in lieu of such demonstration, which will 
expire within 180 Calendar Days of the effective date of its Interconnection Agreement.  SDG&E 
has reflected these modifications in proposed Sections 10.5 and 10.6 of the TO Tariff. 
 
In addition to these requirements, SDG&E proposes time-bound readiness milestones 
throughout the study and interconnection process to help ensure that interconnection requests do 
not remain in the queue indefinitely without demonstrating continued progress: 
 
• 
Election to proceed to the Facilities Study.  After the System Impact Study, an applicant 
must request initiation of the Facilities Study and provide the required deposit; otherwise, 
its application is deemed withdrawn (TO Tariff Sections 10.12.1, 10.13). 
• 
Interconnection Agreement execution.  Following tender of an Interconnection 
Agreement, the ECLL applicant would have thirty (30) days to either execute the 
Interconnection Agreement or request that SDG&E file an unexecuted Interconnection 
Agreement with the Commission.  If the ECLL applicant does neither within the 30-day 
period, its interconnection application would be deemed withdrawn, and the applicant 
would be responsible for reimbursing SDG&E for all costs reasonably incurred to process 
the application that are not otherwise covered by the Study Agreement (TO Tariff Section 
8.1.5).  As with the proposed pro forma Study Agreement, the proposal to include a form 
Interconnection Agreement in SDG&E’s TO Tariff is intended as an over-arching process 
improvement, such that the execution of conforming Interconnection Agreements would 
not require individual filings with, and acceptance by, the Commission.  This will allow

the satisfaction of early milestones to proceed without the need for specific Commission 
action, thereby reducing potential delays for customers and providing the most “shovel-
ready” projects with speed to power for the service requested.   
• 
Limited amendments.  SDG&E proposes to clarify the types of modifications that may 
be made through the existing one-amendment allowance for a Completed Interconnection 
Application.  Permitted modifications include reductions in interconnection service 
capacity, certain changes to project technical parameters or interconnection configuration, 
and modifications to the proposed in-service date or Commercial Operation Date, subject 
to the conditions specified in the proposed TO Tariff.  The proposed revisions also establish 
the timeframe for submitting such an amendment and clarify the applicant’s responsibility 
for any additional study costs resulting from the amendment, including costs associated 
with revisions to studies for later-queued applicants (TO Tariff Section 10.7). 
• 
Security posting.  If the ECLL applicant executes the pro forma Interconnection 
Agreement, the applicant would be required to post the financial security required under 
the Interconnection Agreement by the applicable deadline specified therein.  Failure to 
timely post the required financial security, or any other default under the Interconnection 
Agreement, would result in forfeiture of the applicant’s queue position and withdrawal of 
its interconnection request (TO Tariff Section 10.23). 
Together, these requirements establish clear and enforceable readiness milestones that escalate at 
distinct phases, as the Commission described, and are intended to maintain an actionable queue, 
minimize speculative interconnection requests, and prevent inactive applicants from continuing to 
hold queue positions. 
 
Finally, SDG&E also views the cost responsibility framework, including cost shift 
protections discussed in greater detail below, as critical elements of its proposed readiness 
approach.  In summary, SDG&E’s proposed 100 percent cost-shift protection for network 
upgrades6 (TO Tariff Sections 8.1.2 and 8.1.3 and pro forma IA Articles 11.3, 11.5, and 11.6) and 
advance funding requirement for Direct Assignment Facilities (TO Tariff Section 8.1.2 and pro 
forma IA Articles 5.10 and 11.2) establish clear financial responsibility for interconnection-related 
infrastructure costs at the outset of the interconnection process.  Providing ECLL applicants with 
certainty as to their funding requirements, and the amount and duration of security obligations, 
should help ensure that interconnection requests enter and remain in the queue only where the 
applicant has determined that such funding and security do not jeopardize the commercial viability 
of their planned projects. 
 
3. 
Information and Data Requirements 
 
 
After recognizing that “CAISO and/or the Participating Transmission Owners may have 
existing load integration processes[,]” the Show Cause Order at P 49 expressed:

concern[] that those processes and any required studies … are not described in their 
tariffs with the degree of clarity and specificity necessary to … mitigate operational 
risks…, avoid disputes regarding how studies are conducted, deter speculative or 
duplicative requests…, and help avoid excessive and unnecessary network 
upgrades. 
 
In the months since the issuance of the Show Cause Order, SDG&E has been working in 
conjunction with CAISO, SCE, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (“PG&E”), and other 
stakeholders in the Large Load Technical Requirement Working Group (“LLTRWG”) to develop 
additional technical requirements to be considered in the study process.  Holistically, these 
additional requirements address technical aspects of the ECLL interconnection process and address 
the Commission’s concerns.   
 
SDG&E proposes to modify its TO Tariff to require the ECLL to submit to SDG&E, as 
the PTO, data that the LLTRWG recommends be made available for study and operational 
purposes.  These data include: large load operating characteristics; hourly load profile; ramping 
behavior; power quality; and telemetry and communications data.  Specifically, an ECLL must 
submit the data specified in the System Impact Study Data Template Submittal Form, including 
facility characteristics, load composition and expected hourly operating profile, MW capacity, 
minimum and maximum operating levels, electrical and dynamic model data, voltage and 
frequency ride-through characteristics, protection and control settings, load reconnection behavior, 
expected CAISO market participation model, curtailment and ramping capabilities, and behind-
the-meter generation capacity and characteristics, and must complete CAISO’s Large Load 
Technical Data Request.  An ECLL must also disclose whether substantially similar 
interconnection requests on behalf of the same Large Load have been submitted and whether it is 
requesting Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (“FILI”) Service.   
 
SDG&E has added these data requirements in Section 10.5 of the TO Tariff and 
Attachment B to the pro forma Study Agreement. 
 
C. 
Transmission Service Study 
 
The Show Cause Order notes at P 49 that CAISO and PTO tariffs “do not contain 
provisions addressing with sufficient clarity and consistency how CAISO and/or the Participating 
Transmission Owners will study the provision of transmission service to Eligible Customers on 
behalf of large loads,” and expresses concern at P 51 that “CAISO’s Tariff and/or the TO Tariffs 
may not clearly specify which entity will be responsible for studying the provision of transmission 
service to Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads.”  Later, in paragraph 62 of the Show Cause 
Order, the Commission discusses the need for study processes, and clarity about such processes, 
that include “a report to the Eligible Customer with the results of the studies” that identify “any 
Direct Assignment Facilities and network upgrades necessary to accommodate the transmission 
service request as well as a non-binding good-faith estimate of the cost and the time to construct 
such facilities.”  The study should “recognize … the unique operational characteristics of large

Hon. Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
November 16, 2026

loads” and, the Show Cause Order suggests, should have “a study deadline of no more than 60-90 
calendar days.”  Id. 
 
In response to the Show Cause Order’s concerns, SDG&E clarifies first that with respect 
to requests by an Eligible Customer to interconnect a new project, SDG&E’s TO Tariff already 
outlines the process for both the System Impact Study and the Facilities Study.  Under the existing 
TO Tariff, for instance, “[t]he System Impact Study will identify whether any Direct Assignment 
Facilities or Reliability Upgrades as well as, if applicable, any Delivery Upgrades are necessary to 
deliver a New Facility’s full output over the ISO Controlled Grid.”7  This study process is already 
available for wholesale load interconnection requests by Eligible Customers.  This includes ECLL, 
whether or not a newly-created sub-category of wholesale load called ECLL is created. 
 
In this filing, however, SDG&E proposes revisions to create a new category of Eligible 
Customer called ECLL.  These revisions make abundantly clear that the existing System Impact 
Study and Facilities Study processes apply to the newly-created ECLL customer type, as a new 
category of wholesale load service requested on behalf of a large load, and in recognition of the 
unique technical issues large loads entail, to add an EMT Study where needed.  Thus, for purposes 
of clarity and consistency, SDG&E declares that as the TO, it will, pursuant to the provisions of 
its TO Tariff, conduct the study process that will identify the operating procedures, Direct 
Assignment Facilities, and network upgrades necessary to provide transmission service to an 
ECLL.  Moreover, while not raised in the Show Cause Order, SDG&E commits that it will use the 
same due diligence in completing studies for others as it uses for itself or its affiliates.  The study 
process modifications described here are in in Sections 10.9 through 10.17 of the proposed TO 
Tariff.  Accordingly, SDG&E’s proposed revisions address the Show Cause Order’s concern that 
studies should identify Direct Assignment Facilities as well as network upgrades required to safely 
and reliably interconnect the ECLL is satisfied. 
 
With respect to the unique operational characteristics of large loads, the Show Cause Order 
at P 63 states that existing “tariffs do not require transmission owners to install, and transmission 
customers to pay for, equipment to enable CAISO to monitor large loads for impacts of, for 
example, fast-ramping load that may impact the transmission system too quickly to be captured by 
conventional data acquisition systems (e.g., the need for phasor measurement units or similar 
equipment).”  That same paragraph further observes that the PTO tariffs “do not specify ramp rate 
or ride-through requirements with which the transmission customer taking transmission service on 
behalf of the large load must comply” and do “not specify requirements for necessary control 
technologies and/or protection systems that may be necessary to limit transmission customer’s 
withdrawals from the transmission system as appropriate.” 
 
In response, SDG&E states that it proposes to incorporate the unique operational 
characteristics of Large Loads by implementing the recommendations of the LLTRWG discussed 
above.  In addition, SDG&E notes that at the time of this writing, the LLTRWG initiative has 
already identified CAISO data monitoring requirements (including Phasor Measurement Units

(“PMUs”)), ramp rate and ride-through requirements, and necessary control technologies and 
protection systems.  SDG&E proposes to incorporate these requirements into its process in several 
ways.  First, SDG&E will require that the ECLL submitting an interconnection application provide 
operating characteristics; ramping behavior; and measures to ensure the Large Load does not 
create, or exacerbate, power quality issues on SDG&E’s transmission facilities.  SDG&E has 
added this as an application requirement in Section 10.5 of the proposed TO Tariff.   Second, these 
requirements are captured in the study process in Attachment B of the pro forma Study Agreement 
(Appendix XIII). In particular, the EMT Study scope of work in the Study Agreement covers 
model verification, standalone and integrated simulation, voltage ride-through and load-recovery 
performance, control interactions, sensitivities, and protection and load-tripping response.  Finally, 
SDG&E also proposes that all data and monitoring requirements related to the LLTRWG be 
installed and maintained by the ECLL, as outlined in sections 8.2, 9.6, 9.7.3, 9.7.4, and 9.7.5 of 
SDG&E’s proposed pro forma Interconnection Agreement (Appendix XIV). 
 
 
SDG&E shares the Show Cause Order’s preference for expeditious processing of 
interconnection requests, as evidenced by the Show Cause Order’s suggestion of a 60-90 study 
process to identify Direct Assignment Facilities and network upgrades and provide non-binding 
estimates of cost and time to construct.8  The sooner an Eligible Customer receives its study results, 
the sooner it will be in position to make the business decision regarding whether to make the further 
financial commitments necessary to advance its request further through the process.

decision that best suits its business at each step.  For instance, based on the results of the System

event the ECLL becomes aware that the Large Load will fail to 
reach COD, or will cease operation after COD, the ECLL shall 
promptly notify TO.  The TO may draw the full amount of the 
then-available security at any time the TO has reasonably

any, shall be determined by subtracting the ECLL’s actual Deemed 
Transmission Revenues for the year from that year’s minimum 
requirement, where such subtraction returns a positive result.  The 
amount of such draws shall be recorded in SDG&E’s Transmission 
Revenue Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”) as a credit 
which will reduce TAC rates.

value of those annual requirements equals the estimated present 
value of the forecast lifecycle revenue requirements associated

be calculated for each year as the product of the applicable high 
voltage/low voltage TAC rate and the ECLL’s metered energy 
withdrawals from the transmission grid.  The term “Deemed 
Transmission Revenues” shall mean the product of such 
calculation.  Metering arrangements necessary to determine actual 
deemed transmission revenues, shall be as mutually agreed by the 
ECLL and the TO.

security draws during the current year.

Customer shall promptly provide such additional deposit. 
10.10 Notice of Need for System Impact Study. If the Participating TO and/or 
the ISO, as applicable, determine(s) that a System Impact Study is 
necessary to accommodate the requested Interconnection, the Participating 
TO shall so inform the applicant as soon as practicable. In such cases, the 
Participating TO shall within twenty (20) Business Days of receipt of a 
Completed Interconnection Application, tender a System Impact Study 
Agreement that defines the scope, content, assumptions and terms of 
reference for such study to be completed by the Participating TO; the 
estimated time required to complete it; and such other provisions as the 
parties may reasonably require, and pursuant to which the applicant shall 
agree to reimburse the Participating TO for the reasonable actual costs of 
performing or reviewing the required System Impact Study. A description 
of the Participating TO’s transmission assessment practices for completing 
a System Impact Study is provided in the Participating TO’s FERC Form 
715. Alternatively, if the New Facility Operator will perform the System
Impact Study, the Participating TO shall within twenty (20) Business Days 
of receipt of a Completed Interconnection Application, tender a System

Impact Study Agreement that defines the scope, content, assumptions and 
terms of reference for such study to be reviewed by the Participating TO; 
the estimated time required to complete it; and such other provisions as the 
parties may reasonably require, and pursuant to which the applicant shall 
agree to reimburse the Participating TO for the reasonable actual costs of 
reviewing the required System Impact Study. For an 
Interconnectioninterconnection request to remain a Completed 
Interconnection Application, the applicant shall execute the System 
Impact Study Agreement and return it to the Participating TO within ten 
(10) Business Days together with payment for the reasonable estimated 
cost of the System Impact Study or reviewing the New Facility Operator’s 
System Impact Study. Alternatively, if the applicant requests the 
Participating TO to proceed with the System Impact Study or review 
thereof and commits to abide by the terms, conditions, and cost 
assignments ultimately determined under the ISO ADR Procedures, 
including any determination by FERC or appeal of a FERC determination 
in accordance with that process, the Participating TO shall promptly 
proceed with the System Impact Study provided that such request is 
accompanied by payment for the reasonable estimated cost of the System

resolution under the ISO’s ADR Procedures. If the applicant elects not to 
execute a System Impact Study Agreement, and does not request that the 
Participating TO proceed with the System Impact Study or review thereof,

its application shall be deemed withdrawn, and the applicant shall 
reimburse to the Participating TO all costs reasonably incurred in 
processing the application. 
10.611 System Impact Study Cost Reimbursement. 
10.611.1 
Cost Reimbursement. The System Impact Study Agreement 
shall clearly specify the charge, based on the Participating TO’s 
estimate of the cost and time for completion of the System Impact 
Study. The charge shall not exceed the reasonable actual cost of 
the study. In performing the System Impact Study, the 
Participating TO shall rely, to the extent reasonably practicable, on 
existing transmission planning studies. The applicant will not be 
assessed a charge for such existing studies; however, the applicant 
will be responsible for the reasonable charges associated with any 
modifications to existing planning studies that are reasonably 
necessary to evaluate the impact of the applicant’s request. 
10.69.2 
Multiple Parties. If multiple parties request Interconnection 
at the same location, the Participating TO may conduct a single 
System Impact Study. The costs of that study shall be pro-rated 
among the parties requesting Interconnection. 
10.712 System Impact Study Procedures. Upon receipt of an executed System 
Impact Study Agreement or initiation of the ISO ADR Procedures and 
receipt of payment for estimated study costs, the Participating TO will use 
due diligence to either (a) complete the required System Impact Study

within a sixty (60) day period or (b) complete its review of a New Facility 
Operator’san Eligible Customer’s System Impact Study within thirty (30) 
Calendar Days of its receipt of the completed study. The System Impact 
Study will identity whether any Direct Assignment Facilities or Reliability 
Upgrades as well as, if applicable, any Delivery Upgrades are necessary to 
deliver a New Facility’s full output over the ISO Controlled Grid. The 
System Impact Study will also identify any adverse impact on 
Encumbrances existing as of the applicant’s New Facility 
Operator’sEligible Customer’s Completed Application Date. In the event 
that the Participating TO is unable to complete the required System Impact 
Study within such time period, it shall so notify the applicant, in writing, 
and provide an estimated completion date along with an explanation of the 
reasons why additional time is required to complete the required studies. A 
copy of the completed System Impact Study and related work papers shall 
be made available to the applicant and the ISO. The Participating TO will 
use the same due diligence in completing the System Impact Study for 
others as it uses when completing studies for its affiliateditself as UDC. 
The Participating TO shall notify the applicant and the ISO immediately 
upon completion of the System Impact Study.  The Participating TO may, 
using Good Utility Practice and reasonable engineering judgment, defer 
commencement of a System Impact Study if the study cannot be 
meaningfully completed until results are available for other similarly 
situated or electrically related interconnection requests. The Participating

TO shall notify the applicant of any such deferral. 
10.712.1 
Procedures Upon Completion of System Impact Study. 
Within fifteen (15) Business Days of completion of the System 
Impact Study or review and approval of a New Facility Operator’s 
System Impact Study, the Participating TO shall notify the 
applicant whether the transmission system will be adequate to 
accommodate all of a request for Interconnection. If no costs are 
likely to be incurred for any Direct Assignment Facilities, any 
Reliability Upgrades, or implementing any operating procedures, 
then within thirty (30) Business Days of receipt of the completed

of written approval of the New Facility Operator’s System Impact

request the Participating TO to tender an Interconnection 
Agreement. Within twenty (20) Business Days of such request, the 
Participating TO shall tender to the applicant an Interconnection 
Agreement as provided in Section 8.1.3. If costs are likely to be 
incurred to accommodate a request for Interconnection, then the 
applicant shall request the Participating TO shall tender to the 
applicant perform a Facilities Study Agreement pursuant to Section 
10.8. 
10.810.12.2 
Restudy. The Participating TO may perform a restudy if the 
withdrawal or modification of a higher-queued Interconnection

Request materially affects the results of a completed System

TOInterconnection Customer shall, within fifteen (15) Business Days of

transmission technologies consistent with applicable reliability

10.914 Facilities Study Procedure. Upon receipt of an executedthe applicant’s

such time period, it shall so notify the applicant, in writing, and provide an

additional time is required to complete the required studies. A copy of the 
completed Facilities Study shall be made available to the applicant.

Electromagnetic 
Transient Study. If the Participating TO determines that an

10.16 No Preferential Treatment.  The Participating TO will use the same due 
diligence in completing studies under this tariff for others as it uses for 
itself or its affiliates.

Participating TO shall tender to applicant an Interconnection Agreement

the Participating TO determines that there will not be adequate

and provide the portion of the requested Interconnection that can be 
accommodated without any additional Direct Assignment Facilities or 
Reliability Upgrades. However, the Participating TO shall not be obligated 
to provide the incremental amount of requested Interconnection that 
requires such additional facilities or upgrades to the transmission system 
until such facilities or upgrades have been placed in service. 
10.1119 
Expedited Interconnection Procedures. In lieu of the procedures set 
forth above, the applicant shall have the option to expedite the processing 
of its Completed Interconnection Application. In order to exercise this 
option, the applicant shall submit in writing a Request for Expedited 
Interconnection Procedures to the Participating TO, and to the ISO, if the 
applicant is a New Facility Operator, within ten (10) Business Days after 
receiving a copy of the System Impact Study for the proposed 
Interconnection. Within ten (10) Business Days after receiving a Request 
for Expedited Procedures, the Participating TO shall tender an Expedited 
Interconnection Agreement that requires the applicant to compensate the 
Participating TO for all costs reasonably incurred pursuant to the terms of 
this TO Tariff for processing the Completed Interconnection Application 
and providing the requested Interconnection. While the Participating TO 
agrees to provide the applicant with its best estimate of the costs of any

needed Direct Assignment Facilities and, if applicable, Reliability 
Upgrades and other charges that may be incurred, unless otherwise agreed 
by the parties, such estimate shall not be binding and the applicant must 
agree in writing to compensate the Participating TO for all actual 
interconnection costs reasonably incurred pursuant to the provisions of 
this TO Tariff. The applicant shall execute and return such Expedited 
Interconnection Agreement within ten (10) Business Days of its receipt or 
the applicant’s request for Interconnection will cease to be a Completed 
Interconnection Application and will be deemed terminated and 
withdrawn. In that event, the applicant shall reimburse the Participating 
TO for all costs reasonably incurred in processing the application not 
covered by the terms of the System Impact Study Agreement.Study 
Agreement. 
10.20 Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (“FILI”) Service For ECLL.  If the 
ECLL is requesting FILI Service, the TO shall perform, as part of the 
System Impact Study, an analysis and determine the portion of the 
ECLL’s maximum operating level that may be energized prior to such 
time that all network upgrades necessary for full energization of the 
studied loads are in service.  The portion that may be energized will be 
documented in the executed and effective Interconnection Agreement.   
 
Pursuant to Section 25.7.1 of the ISO Tariff, the ECLL may be required to 
execute an agreement with the ISO and TO if real-time operating 
procedures are necessary to effectuate the limit determined by the TO in

this Section 10.20.  Such agreement will describe the circumstances in 
which the Large Load may be temporarily curtailed and the mechanism 
used to perform the curtailment.  
10.21 Conditions Related to FILI Service For ECLL. 
10.21.1 
FILI Service Reliability Requirements. The Participating 
TO shall have sole discretion to specify the protection, control 
systems and any other equipment necessary to ensure the Large 
Load does not withdraw more power from the ISO Controlled Grid 
than allowed by the limit established pursuant to Section 10.20.  
The required protection, control systems and other equipment; and 
the party responsible for installing, owning and maintaining those 
systems and equipment; will be identified in the Interconnection 
Agreement.  FILI Service shall not commence until the 
installation and commissioning of all systems and equipment 
identified in the Interconnection Agreement has been completed. 
10.21.2 
Curtailment of FILI Service.  The TO and ISO may curtail 
FILI Service as necessary to maintain the safe and reliable 
operation of the ISO Controlled Grid, including during normal 
operating conditions. 
10.21.3 
Exceedance of Authorized FILI Service.  The TO shall 
have the right to disconnect service to the ECLL in the event that 
withdrawals from the ISO Controlled Grid exceed the limit 
established pursuant to Section 10.20. The TO shall follow Good

Utility Practice in carrying out any such disconnection and 
subsequent reconnection.    
10.22 Co-Located Generation Units and Large Loads. ECLL for a Co-Located 
Large Load connecting to facilities of an exporting Generating Facilities 
will be subject to this Section 10.22.  The CAISO and the Participating 
TO will publish study results reflecting the combined presence of the 
Generating Units and co-located Large Loads.  The CAISO and SDG&E 
will memorialize the result of such studies in a Large Generation 
Interconnection Agreement (LGIA) with the New Facility Operator.  For 
clarity, the New Facility Operator may be the same legal entity as either 
the ECLL or the Large Load, but not both.  The Participating TO’s 
System Impact Study shall consider co-located generation to the extent it 
does not export power to the ISO Controlled Grid.  Any requested export 
service shall be addressed under the applicable generator interconnection 
procedures of the ISO Tariff.  
In the event of a conflict between the CAISO Tariff and this TO 
Tariff pertaining to the interconnection of the Generating Unit, the CAISO 
Tariff shall control.  In the event of a conflict between the CAISO Tariff 
and this TO Tariff pertaining to the interconnection of an ECLL, this TO 
Tariff shall control.  Nothing in the CAISO Tariff shall be interpreted to 
contradict or exempt an ECLL from its cost responsibility obligations 
pursuant to this TO Tariff, and nothing in this TO Tariff shall be 
interpreted to contradict or exempt a New Facility Operator from its cost

responsibility obligations pursuant to the CAISO Tariff.     
10.23 Effect of Default Under Interconnection Agreement.  Interconnection 
Customer shall forfeit its queue position and its Completed 
Interconnection Application shall be deemed withdrawn with respect to 
any Project as to which Interconnection Customer is in default under the 
applicable Interconnection Agreement, including without limitation failure 
to provide required security.
